summary.headline: Rashi Peripherals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 62% YoY to Rs 5,102 crore, with PAT up 69% to Rs 105 crore and ROCE near 19.5%.
summary.overview: Management reported record consolidated revenue, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE for the quarter ended June 2026, driven by price increases in memory, storage and CPUs plus a rise in unit volume. Management said about 30-35% of the revenue growth came from price, 20-25% from quantity, 5-10% from new products and brands, and about 10% from market share gains. Pillars cited were the core distribution engine, the VDA Infosolutions acquisition (67% stake) and a semiconductor JV with Restar Japan (74:26). Management guided to similar growth in Q2 but a slower pace of price increases.

financial_highlights.change: up 55% YoY (CEO cited 50% on the opening remarks)

segments.name: Consolidated group
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 5,102 crore and PAT Rs 105 crore; management stated all-time highs on topline, EBITDA, PAT and annualised ROCE.

segments.name: Commercial vs consumer (B2B mix)
segments.commentary: Management estimates 30-35% consumer-centric and 60-65% commercial (SMB and enterprise). Consumer demand is slowing on affordability, with laptop prices reportedly about 2x year-on-year.

segments.name: Semiconductor / embedded
segments.commentary: Semiconductor revenue in Q1 grew about 70% versus the Q1 FY26 base (not 70% of full-year revenue, per clarification). Growth is described as near double-digit and sometimes higher.

segments.name: VDA Infosolutions (acquired)
segments.commentary: Majority stake (67% in year one) in a pan-India system integrator; FY26 revenue was about Rs 850 crore. Management expects integrated services and value-added solutions to be about 5% of revenue, with Q2 as the next update point.

guidance_outlook: Q2 FY27 growth expected to be similar to Q1 (about 60%), with price increase speed roughly halving; management described Q2 as on a strong footing.
Management expects the price uptrend to continue through FY27, with some slowdown in trajectory.
Management cited third-party reports of about a 10% unit decline in the overall PC market, offset by price increases.
Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record over 20 years; cited about Rs 3,000 crore as 20% of a Rs 16,000 crore base.
Semiconductor JV targets more than US$100 million revenue within three years; the JV numbers will be reported with Q2 results.
Large AI data centre deals not pursued aggressively in Q1 due to working-capital needs; management said the pipeline should last at least three quarters.
capex_capacity: Two new branches planned in Udaipur and Dhule to extend reach into C and D class cities.
Presence across 57 towns in India, per management.
Semiconductor JV Rashi Restar Semiconductor Solutions Private Limited to be formed as a step-down subsidiary; Restar to take 26% stake, with the existing embedded business moving into the JV.
Plans to add 50+ local engineering hires over the next two years for the semiconductor JV.
Debt-to-equity ratio cited at around 0.5; management said large data centre projects could push it to at least 2x.
demand_pricing: Memory, hard drive and CPU shortages are pushing prices higher; management expects the uptrend to continue through FY27.
Management said about 10% market share gain contributed to growth; unit growth ex-SanDisk was about 20%, with SanDisk unit declines pulling reported units lower.
Entry-level laptops face about 50% shortage per management; medium and premium notebooks available if prices are accepted.
T2 partners are holding elevated channel inventory to earn double-digit margins; management said it is not a concern given demand.
Refurbished PCs are seen as small: management estimated the refurbished pool at 0.5-1 million units against a 15-16 million PC TAM in India.
Management said Dell commercial business contributed about 5% of revenue in the quarter, and is above target for FY27.
Management said the company has allocations from NVIDIA, Intel and AMD; supply risk is tracked weekly ('orange alert').

qa_highlights.question: Why is India demand strong relative to global peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited economic strength, digitisation and education focus, plus data centre-related demand; commercial demand is holding up while consumer demand is slowing on affordability.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth between price, volume and mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Price 30-35%, quantity 20-25%, new products and brands 5-10%, market share about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 growth match Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 should show a similar trend (about 60%), but the speed of price increases should roughly halve.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline: price or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix (higher PES share, lower margin than LIT) and to last year's hived-off subsidiary whose service cost sat in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a supply constraint risk in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is potential risk, but allocations so far are good given supplier relationships; the company tracks it weekly.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue large AI data centre deals aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritised run-rate business with higher ROCE and working-capital needs; it still participates through smaller Rs 20-70 crore supplies and focuses on neo-clouds and smaller operators.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY28 look after the tailwinds fade?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% CAGR track record and cited VDA and the Restar JV as longer-term growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Semiconductor JV economics and Restar's investment amount?
qa_highlights.answer: Restar's investment depends on fair valuation at SPA signing, so it is not quantified; management targets over US$100 million JV revenue in three years and said the JV margin profile is higher than co-distribution.
